questions.stemHtml: A patient presents with abdominal pain. On examination, there is a mass palpable in the right hypochondrium. Ultrasound showed a cystic lesion in the liver. USG-guided aspiration was done and microscopy of the aspirate is shown. What is the likely infection in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Echinococcus granulosus
  • Echinococcus granulosus causes hydatid disease, which is characterized by the formation of cysts, typically in the liver (right hypochondrium), as seen in this patient. The cystic lesion is visible on ultrasound, and the image of the aspirate shows hydatid cysts with scolices (hooks) inside, which is diagnostic.
  • The infection is transmitted through canine feces (dogs), and involves ingestion of the eggs, which leads to cyst formation in organs like the liver and lungs.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 350

questions.stem: Which of the following is not involved in development of a naïve T cell to an activated helper T cell?

options.label: C
options.text: PD1 on T cell interaction with PD-L1 on APC

questions.answerText: PD1 on T cell interaction with PD-L1 on APC
questions.solutionHtml:
PD1 on T cell interaction with PD-L1 on APC
  • The interaction between PD1 on T cells and PD-L1 on APCs is a mechanism of immune regulation and immune checkpoint inhibition. It serves to downregulate immune responses, promoting tolerance rather than activation. Therefore, this interaction does not contribute to the activation of naïve T cells into helper T cells.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 349-350

questions.stem: Bacteriological loops used for culture media inoculation are sterilized by which of the following methods?

options.label: C
options.text: Placing in flame until it becomes red hot

questions.answerText: Placing in flame until it becomes red hot
questions.solutionHtml:
Placing in flame until it becomes red hot
  • Bacteriological loops are sterilized by heating them until they become red hot in a flame. This ensures the destruction of any microorganisms on the loop, preventing contamination during inoculation.

Why the Flame Until Red Hot?

  • The heat denatures the proteins and nucleic acids of any potential microorganisms, rendering them non-viable.
  • This method is quick, effective, and ideal for small metal instruments like bacteriological loops


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 60

questions.stem: A 20-year-old develops a pustule progressed quickly to necrotizing fasciitis. Gram positive cocci in chains were seen on microscopy of the exudate. Which of the following is the most likely aetiology?
questions.solutionHtml:
Streptococcus pyogenes
  • The most likely aetiology of necrotizing fasciitis with Gram-positive cocci in chains is Streptococcus pyogenes. This bacterium is known for causing severe soft tissue infections like necrotizing fasciitis.
  • The exotoxins produced by Streptococcus pyogenes lead to rapid tissue destruction and systemic toxicity, resulting in severe complications like toxic shock syndrome. Necrotizing fasciitis often progresses quickly and can be life-threatening.

Streptococci in Gram stain stained smear




Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 177

questions.stemHtml: Farmer comes with a wound acquired a couple of weeks back following a blunt trauma from a farming tool. Microscopy of the wound exudate showed weakly acid-fast beaded filamentous rods as shown in the figure. What is the most likely aetiology of this infection?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nocardia
  • Nocardia is the most likely causative agent because it is weakly acid-fast and forms beaded, filamentous rods under the microscope. This organism is typically acquired after trauma, especially in people exposed to soil (such as farmers). It causes cutaneous infections, which aligns with the patient's history of blunt trauma from a farming tool.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 108

questions.stem: Which of the following when administered to a patient does not impart passive immunity?
questions.solutionHtml:
Toxoid
  • Toxoid does not impart passive immunity. It is a modified toxin that is rendered non-toxic but still immunogenic. Toxoids are used for active immunization, stimulating the body to produce its own antibodies.
  • Passive immunity, on the other hand, involves the direct transfer of antibodies or immune cells from one individual to another, and toxoids do not provide this form of immunity.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 52

questions.stem: Which culture medium is used for isolation of MTB?
questions.solutionHtml:
LJ medium
  • Lowenstein-Jensen (LJ) medium is the most commonly used medium for the isolation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB). It is a selective medium containing malachite green, which inhibits the growth of contaminants while promoting the growth of MTB.
  • LJ Medium is solid, provides necessary nutrients, and supports the slow-growing nature of MTB.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 245

questions.stem: Which of the following is a test for carrying out antibiotic sensitivity?
questions.solutionHtml:
E-test
  • The E-test (also known as the epsilometer test) is a method used for determining the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of antibiotics. It uses a strip impregnated with a gradient of an antibiotic, and the point at which bacterial growth is inhibited indicates the MIC, providing a precise measure of antibiotic sensitivity.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 151

questions.stemHtml: Match the disease with the aetiological agent:Select the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3
  • Statement: A. Donovanosis: Caused by Klebsiella granulomatis, resulting in genital ulcers and granulomatous tissue.
  • Statement: B. Oroya Fever: Caused by Bartonella bacilliformis, transmitted by sandflies, leading to severe anemia.
  • Statement: C. Rat Bite Fever: Caused by Streptobacillus moniliformis, a bacterium transmitted by rat bites or scratches.
  • Statement: D. Pinta: Caused by Treponema carateum, a spirochete related to syphilis, but causing a chronic skin disease.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 252

questions.stem: Which of the following cancers can be prevented by vaccination?Cervical cancerBurkitt lymphomaMerkel cell carcinomaHepatocellular carcinomaSelect the correct the Answer from the given below Code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1 and 4 only
  • Cervical cancer (a) is primarily caused by Human Papillomavirus (HPV), and vaccination against HPV (like the Gardasil vaccine) can prevent the development of this cancer.
  • Hepatocellular carcinoma (d) is mainly caused by chronic infection with Hepatitis B and C viruses. Vaccination against Hepatitis B (HBV) reduces the risk of developing this cancer.
  • Both of these cancers (cervical cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma) can thus be prevented by vaccination.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 342

questions.stem: A farmer presents with swelling of foot. He gives a history of always walking barefoot. On Examination there are multiple ulcers/sinuses. Which of the following infection could have been acquired by the farmer due to walking barefoot?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mycetoma
  • Mycetoma is a chronic granulomatous infection commonly acquired by walking barefoot, especially in tropical or subtropical regions. It is caused by either fungi (eumycetoma) or bacteria (actinomycetoma) and is characterized by:
    • Swelling, discharging sinuses, and grain production.
    • Common causative agents: Madurella, Nocardia, and Actinomadura.
    • The mode of acquisition involves traumatic inoculation of the organism into the skin.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 640

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about Cryptococcus:Pathogenic species are urease positiveC. Gattii is associated with bird guanoExtrapulmonary cryptococcosis is an AIDS-defining illnessOpportunistic infection is seen in AIDS when CD4 counts fall below 500Select the correct answer from the Given below Code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1, 3
  • Statement: 1.Pathogenic species are urease positive: Cryptococcus species, especially C. neoformans, are urease-positive, which aids in the identification of the pathogen.
  • Statement: 3.Extrapulmonary cryptococcosis is an AIDS-defining illness: Extrapulmonary cryptococcosis, particularly cryptococcal meningitis, is considered an AIDS-defining illness when CD4 counts fall below 100.
  • Statement: 2. Gatti is associated with bird guano: While C. Gatti can be found in the environment, it is not primarily associated with bird guano. It is more commonly found in eucalyptus trees in tropical areas.
  • Statement: 4. Opportunistic infection is seen in AIDS when CD4 counts fall below 500: Cryptococcus typically causes severe infections when CD4 counts fall below 100, not 500.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 707

questions.stem: A 2-Year-old child presents with watery Diarrhoea for last 3 days. On examination the baby is severely dehydrated. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
questions.solutionHtml:
Rotavirus
  • Rotavirus is the most common cause of severe watery diarrhea in children under 5 years, particularly in developing countries. Key points:
  • Transmission:
    • Fecal-oral route.
  • Pathogenesis:
    • Virus infects enterocytes, causing malabsorption and secretory diarrhea.
  • Clinical Features:
    • Watery diarrhea lasting 4-8 days.
    • Vomiting and fever are common.
    • Severe dehydration may develop, especially in young children.
  • Prevention:
    • Vaccination significantly reduces morbidity and mortality.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 725.

questions.stem: A child is brought to the emergency with complaints of diarrhoea for last 3 days and now blood in urine. Investigations reveal thrombocytopenia. Stool culture would likely isolate?
questions.solutionHtml:
E. Coli 0157:H7 / EHEC
  • Coli O157:H7, a strain of Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EHEC), is known to cause Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS), which is characterized by:
  • Thrombocytopenia, renal failure, and hemolytic anemia. This strain often presents with bloody diarrhea and can lead to kidney damage, which aligns with the child's symptoms of blood in urine and thrombocytopenia.
  • EHEC is commonly associated with contaminated food, particularly undercooked beef.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 674

options.label: D
options.text: Asthma-like conditions can be seen following infection

questions.answerText: Massive infection can cause rectal prolapse
questions.solutionHtml:
Massive infection can cause rectal prolapse
  • While rectal prolapse is a complication that can occur in certain gastrointestinal infections, it is not typically associated with Ascaris lumbricoides.
  • In fact, massive infections with Ascaris are more commonly linked to intestinal obstruction, not prolapse. The worms can cause a mechanical obstruction in the intestines, leading to symptoms like abdominal pain, vomiting, and distention, particularly in children.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 426
